To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Beltaos’ (2018) regression analysis of ice-jam floods overestimates flood frequency and is therefore not a reliable indicator of change in flood frequency; 2) the observed decrease in flood frequency after 1971 cannot be attributed to the WAC Bennett dam; and 3) the observed decrease is likely a result of natural climate variability, which is consistent with independent, paleo-hydrologic reconstructions.

(1) ice-jam flood frequencies in the lower Peace-Athabaca Delta have been relatively constant since 1880, (2) the frequency of ice-jam floods has been relatively constant in both the pre- and post-regulation periods, (3) the frequency of large ice-jams in the lower Peace is not increasing, (4) the frequency of small ice-jams is decreasing, and (5) the observed decrease in the frequency of small floods is not a result of

1) there was a significant increase in flood frequency after 1968, 2) this increase was not due to a decrease in flood magnitude (as shown by Beltaos 1995, 2018), and 3) the increase in flood frequency cannot be explained by hydrological regulation of the Peace-A thabasca River (as shown by Wolfe et al. 2013, 2014).
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of hydrological change on the drying of lakes in the Peace–Athabasca Delta (PADD) in northern Alberta, Canada.
the role of ice-jam floods on lake levels and water budgets in the Peace-Arbasca Delta.

understanding the hydrological history of the PAD, which is the most extensive freshwater wetland in North America (Kuzyk and Kokelj 2019), and the role of climate and human activities in driving changes in lake levels, lake area, and lake water balance (e.g., Wolfe et al. 2010, 2012, 2013, 2014).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed increase in the frequency of ice-jam floods on the Peace River after 1971 is not statistically different from what might have been expected from the pre-regulation period.
there is no evidence that the frequency of large Peace River ice-jam floods has changed since 1967.
the frequency of major floods has decreased over the last 100 years, and that the decrease is not statistically different between the pre- and post-dam periods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are many factors influencing the hydrology and ecology of the Peace-Atha-basca Delta.
the Peace-Athbasca Delta is a complex system with many interacting factors, which makes it very difficult to isolate the effects of any one factor.
there is a need to understand the history of hydrologic change in the PAD, including the influence of ice-jam floods and regulation of the Peace-Ambaska Delta.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it does not support a conclusion that the Peace-Athbasca Delta has dried as a consequence of regulation of the Peace-Arbasca River by the W.A.C. Bennett dam,
the observed frequency of ice-jam floods has not changed since 1967.
the frequency and magnitude of floods in the Peace River have not changed in recent decades, and thus cannot be a factor that has led to drying in the Peace-Atha-basca Delta.
